= Pinmux: FPV Testplan
:toc: left

The testpoints of the pinmux formal property verification (FPV): every requirement of the
link:{da}[design architecture doc] as a rule over the xref:{tp}#definitions[Terms], named checks in both
directions, the cases the tool must reach, the edge cases, what must never happen and the run
that checks it. The link:../tb_arch/pinmux_tb_arch.adoc[TB architecture doc] turns each check into
a property. The design is the pinmux as instanced in Earlgrey.

== Overview

[[how_to_read]]
=== How to read it

Each testpoint states its rule in plain English sentences over the xref:{tp}#definitions[Terms] and the cases a cover must reach.
Checks and cases have names in italics; the TB architecture doc's check map links each check to its property. An assert
decides each outcome; a cover only shows that a case is reachable.

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds
|Requirements |The requirements the testpoint closes; each is in exactly one testpoint
|Rule |The expected behaviour in plain English over the Terms, each condition, value and cycle exact, with the condition that hands a case to another testpoint
|Observed at |The ports and register values the checks read
|Checks |One assertion per row, named by what it guarantees, with its type
|Cases, truth table |A base case, then one input varied per row; one row per condition, each naming the check that decides it
|Edge cases, Never |Boundary values; what must never happen, each with its deciding check and its witness: a case or truth-table row of the testpoint, or a row of xref:{tp}#witnesses[Consistency witnesses] where another testpoint decides the output
|Run, Blocked by |The run (xref:{tp}#run_variants[Run variants]) that reaches it; the readings an expected value rests on
|===

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Type |Meaning
|forward |The design responds when the rule says so, within the rule's window
|backward |The design responds only then: no response the rule did not call for
|legal |The spec's answer to an illegal or out-of-range value, and only then
|stable |What must not change: a locked value, a held pad, a sticky bit
|===

A testpoint closed by composition has *Follows from* instead of checks: the requirements it
follows from and its premises. One decided in another plan names that plan.

=== Testpoint map and status

*Rule:* each pinmux block is proven in one checker, its testpoints under it.

== Input selection

=== How it works

*Rule:* each MIO input reads what its input select names, each DIO input its pad, in the same cycle
(xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#input_selection[Input selection], design doc).
<<tp_pad_listen,pad_listen>> decides both; xref:{tp}#tp_reset_state[reset_state] composes reset.

[[tp_pad_listen]]
=== pad_listen: every peripheral input reads what its select names

*Rule:* in every cycle, every MIO input (`mio_to_periph_o`) reads its selected input value (xref:{tp}#defs_pads[Pads, selection, sleep, attributes, locks and bus]), unless
the pad its input select names is an owned JTAG pad in that cycle, and every DIO input (`dio_to_periph_o`) reads its
own pad (`dio_in_i`) ([REG] hjson:469-470; [TP] InSel0_A to InSelOOB_A, DioInSelN_A). On the EG2 top only where the
input select is not unlisted (xref:{tp}#tp_sparse_insel[sparse_insel] decides the rest). *Observed at:* the peripheral inputs, the pad inputs, the input selects.

Checks and truth table, one cover per row; the classes cover 0 to 63, each an equality (backward).

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,2,1,2,3"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |Select |Expected
|[[chk_pad_listen_01]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_01` |reads tie 0 |forward |0 |0 (REQ_IN_01)
|[[chk_pad_listen_02]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_02` |reads tie 1 |forward |1 |1 (REQ_IN_02)
|[[chk_pad_listen_03]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_03` |reads selected pad |forward |2 to 48, per pad |MIO pad number select minus 2 on `mio_in_i`, same cycle (REQ_IN_03)
|[[chk_pad_listen_04]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_04` |no pad reads 0 |legal |49 to 63 |0 (REQ_IN_04)
|[[chk_pad_listen_05]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_05` |DIO reads its pad |forward |none, per DIO pad |its own pad (`dio_in_i`), whatever the registers hold (REQ_IN_05)
|[[chk_pad_listen_06]]`CHK_PAD_LISTEN_06` |no claim here |none |`2 + p` naming an owned JTAG pad |none: either value meets the spec (reading RD43)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|An input tied to 0 (xref:{reqs}#req_in_01[`REQ_IN_01`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|1 (xref:{reqs}#req_in_02[`REQ_IN_02`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Reading the selected pad (xref:{reqs}#req_in_03[`REQ_IN_03`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A select naming no pad (xref:{reqs}#req_in_04[`REQ_IN_04`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A DIO input (xref:{reqs}#req_in_05[`REQ_IN_05`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_pad select_ (base) |input 78 (UART0 receive) selects 27: pad 25 (IOC3) |`mio_in_i[25]`; _reads selected pad_
|_one-cycle pulse_ |pad 25 low for one cycle |input 78 low in that cycle only; _reads selected pad_
|_other pad moves_ |pad 26 changes |input 78 unchanged; _reads selected pad_
|_shared pad_ |inputs 0 and 96 select 27 too |all three read pad 25; _reads selected pad_
|_select change_ |the select becomes 28 |pad 26 from the cycle the register holds 28; _reads selected pad_
|_DIO input_ |DIO 3 changes, any register values |`dio_to_periph_o[3]` follows; _DIO reads its pad_
|===

*Edge cases:* selects 2, 48, 49, 63; inputs 0 and 96; the JTAG pads (selects 37 to 41) with no
TAP connected; pad 30 (TAP strap 0) as an input; DIO 0 and 15. +
*Never:* an input reads a pad it does not select, or a cycle late (_reads selected pad_; witness
_EG2 unlisted pair_, _one-cycle pulse_); a select naming no pad reads a pad (_no pad reads 0_;
witness its row); a DIO input reads another pad or depends on a register (_DIO reads its pad_;
witness _DIO input_).

*Run:* V1, every select value reachable. *Blocked by:* none; readings RD1, RD2.

== Pad output

ifndef::tp[:tp: pinmux_fpv_testplan.adoc]
=== Testpoints of the pad output

[%header,cols="1,4"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks
|<<tp_pad_output,pad_output>> |An awake pad drives what its select names
|<<tp_pad_sleep,pad_sleep>> |An asleep pad drives its sleep value until software clears its bit
|<<tp_pad_attr,pad_attr>> |Every pad gets the attributes its register reads back
|===

Design doc:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#output_selection[Output selection],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#sleep_retention[Sleep retention],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#pad_attributes[Pad attributes]. Precedence: an awake
pad's drive is <<tp_pad_output,pad_output>>'s, an asleep one's <<tp_pad_sleep,pad_sleep>>'s, the
attributes <<tp_pad_attr,pad_attr>>'s; an owned JTAG pad is the JTAG pad testpoints' (readings RD43, RD44).

[[tp_pad_output]]
=== pad_output: every awake pad drives what its select names

*Rule:* in every cycle, an awake MIO pad that is not an owned JTAG pad drives its selected drive
(Terms: xref:{tp}#defs_pads[Pads, selection, sleep, attributes, locks and bus]); an
awake DIO pad drives its selected drive, its own peripheral ([REG] hjson:514-515; [ToO]:74; [TP] OutSel0_A to OutSelOeOOB_A, DOutSelN_A,
DOutSelOeN_A). On the EG2 top (what EG2 is: xref:{da}#eg2_changes[design doc, EG2 changes]) only where the output
select is listed (xref:{tp}#tp_sparse_outsel[sparse_outsel]). *Observed at:* the pad outputs and enables, the peripheral outputs and enables,
the output selects, the status bits.

Checks and truth table, one cover per row. The classes cover selects 0 to 127 and each is an
equality, so together the forward checks also give the backward direction.

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,2,1,2,3"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |Select |Expected (out, oe)
|[[chk_pad_output_01]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_01` |tie 0 drives 0 |forward |0 |(0, 1) (REQ_OUT_01a and REQ_OUT_01b)
|[[chk_pad_output_02]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_02` |tie 1 drives 1 |forward |1 |(1, 1) (REQ_OUT_02a and REQ_OUT_02b)
|[[chk_pad_output_03]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_03` |select 2 is high-Z |forward |2 |(0, 0) (REQ_OUT_03a and REQ_OUT_03b)
|[[chk_pad_output_04]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_04` |drives selected output |forward |3 to 108, per output |(`periph_to_mio_i[k]`, `periph_to_mio_oe_i[k]`), same cycle (REQ_OUT_04a and REQ_OUT_04b)
|[[chk_pad_output_05]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_05` |no output is high-Z |legal |109 to 127 |(0, 0) (REQ_OUT_05a and REQ_OUT_05b)
|[[chk_pad_output_06]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_06` |DIO drives its peripheral |forward |none, per DIO pad |the DIO pad's selected drive (REQ_OUT_06a and REQ_OUT_06b)
|[[chk_pad_output_07]]`CHK_PAD_OUTPUT_07` |no claim here |none |asleep, or an owned JTAG pad |pad_sleep; the JTAG pad testpoints
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 0. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_01a[`REQ_OUT_01a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 0, so the pad drives 0. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_01b[`REQ_OUT_01b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_02a[`REQ_OUT_02a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 1, so the pad drives 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_02b[`REQ_OUT_02b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 2: the pad is high-Z. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_03a[`REQ_OUT_03a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 2. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_03b[`REQ_OUT_03b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|MIO pad `p` shall carry peripheral output `k`, in the same cycle, while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 3 + `k` (`k` from 0 to 105). (xref:{reqs}#req_out_04a[`REQ_OUT_04a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|MIO pad `p` shall carry output enable `k`, in the same cycle, while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 3 + `k` (`k` from 0 to 105). (xref:{reqs}#req_out_04b[`REQ_OUT_04b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 109 to 127, the values that name no peripheral output: the pad is high-Z. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_05a[`REQ_OUT_05a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 109 to 127, the values that name no peripheral output. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_05b[`REQ_OUT_05b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|DIO pad `d` shall carry its peripheral's output, in the same cycle. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_06a[`REQ_OUT_06a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|DIO pad `d` shall carry its peripheral's output enable, in the same cycle. (xref:{reqs}#req_out_06b[`REQ_OUT_06b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_peripheral select_ (base) |pad 26 (IOC4) selects 81, any attributes: UART0 transmit (output 78) drives 1, enable 1 |(1, 1); _drives selected output_
|_enable drops_ |enable 78 falls |`mio_oe_o[26]` falls in the same cycle, data still output 78; _drives selected output_
|_one-cycle pulse_ |output 78 at 0 for one cycle |`mio_out_o[26]` 0 in that cycle only; _drives selected output_
|_neighbour moves_ |output 79 and its enable change |pad 26 unchanged; _drives selected output_
|_no output_ |select 110 |(0, 0) whatever output 78 does; _no output is high-Z_
|_DIO pad_ |DIO 3 (SPI_HOST_D1): its peripheral changes |follows in the same cycle; _DIO drives its peripheral_
|_after release_ |pad 26's status bit cleared |pad 26's selected drive from the cycle the bit is 0; _drives selected output_
|===

*Edge cases:* selects 3, 108, 109, 127; pads 0 and 46; the JTAG pads with no TAP connected; the
entry cycle (the bit is still 0: the pad follows its select); DIO 0 and 15. +
*Never:* a pad carries the data of one output with the enable of another, or lags its select by a
cycle (_drives selected output_; reached in _sleep over select_); a high-Z or no-output select drives,
or puts 1 on the output (_select 2 is high-Z_, _no output is high-Z_; reached in _no output_); an
awake DIO pad carries anything but its peripheral (_DIO drives its peripheral_; reached in _DIO pad_);
an attribute changes a pad's output or enable (every check: the selected drive involves no attribute; reached in
the base case, any attributes).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none; readings: same cycle
(RD1), the first value that names nothing
(RD2).

[[tp_pad_sleep]]
=== pad_sleep: a pad takes its sleep mode at sleep entry and holds it until software releases it

*Rule:* for every MIO and DIO pad, in every cycle: the status bit takes, in the next cycle, the next value the truth
table below gives it; and an
asleep pad with a sleep mode taken drives its sleep value, by that mode, in the same
cycle ([REG] hjson:745-748, 790-797, 821-837; [RG]:879, 887; readings RD37, RD40; [TP] MioSleepMode0_A to DioOeSleepStable_A).
*Observed at:* the status bits as the register block holds them, `sleep_en_i`, the sleep registers, the status writes on `tl_i`, what each pad drives.

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,2,1,6"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_pad_sleep_01]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_01` |bit set at entry |forward |a sleep entry with the pad's sleep enable at 1 and no software clear of the status bit gives status bit 1 in the next cycle (REQ_SLP_01)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_02]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_02` |bit set only at entry |backward |the status bit goes from 0 to 1 only in the next cycle after a sleep entry with the pad's sleep enable at 1 (REQ_SLP_02)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_03]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_03` |bit holds until cleared |stable |a status bit at 1 with no software clear of it in a cycle is 1 in the next cycle, whatever `sleep_en_i`, the pad's sleep enable and the peripherals do (REQ_SLP_07)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_04]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_04` |clear releases |forward |a software clear of the status bit in a cycle gives status bit 0 in the next cycle (REQ_SLP_07)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_05]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_05` |clear wins |forward |a software clear of the status bit in a cycle with a sleep entry and the pad's sleep enable at 1 gives status bit 0 in the next cycle (REQ_SLP_09)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_06]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_06` |tie low in sleep |forward |mode taken 0: (0, 1) (REQ_SLP_03a and REQ_SLP_03b)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_07]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_07` |tie high in sleep |forward |mode taken 1: (1, 1) (REQ_SLP_04a and REQ_SLP_04b)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_08]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_08` |high-Z in sleep |forward |mode taken 2: (0, 0) (REQ_SLP_05a and REQ_SLP_05b)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_09]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_09` |keep holds |stable |mode taken 3: the held value (REQ_SLP_06a and REQ_SLP_06b)
|[[chk_pad_sleep_10]]`CHK_PAD_SLEEP_10` |mode write while held |stable |a write to the sleep mode while the status bit is 1 leaves the pad's drive as it is: it still drives the sleep value of the mode taken (REQ_SLP_10a and REQ_SLP_10b; reading RD40)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|At sleep entry, the status bit of every pad whose sleep enable is 1 shall become 1, unless a software clear of that bit lands in the same cycle (`REQ_SLP_09`). (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_01[`REQ_SLP_01`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A status bit shall become 1 only at sleep entry, and only if the pad's sleep enable is 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_02[`REQ_SLP_02`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 0, a pad's output shall be 0. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_03a[`REQ_SLP_03a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 0, a pad's output enable shall be 1, so the pad drives 0. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_03b[`REQ_SLP_03b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 1, a pad's output shall be 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_04a[`REQ_SLP_04a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 1, a pad's output enable shall be 1, so the pad drives 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_04b[`REQ_SLP_04b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 2, a pad's output enable shall be 0: the pad is high-Z. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_05a[`REQ_SLP_05a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 2, a pad's output shall be 0. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_05b[`REQ_SLP_05b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 3, a pad shall keep the output it drove in the last cycle before the bit became 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_06a[`REQ_SLP_06a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 3, a pad shall keep the output enable it drove in the last cycle before the bit became 1. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_06b[`REQ_SLP_06b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Once 1, a status bit shall stay 1 until software writes 0 to it, whatever `sleep_en_i`, the sleep enable and the peripheral do. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_07[`REQ_SLP_07`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|When sleep entry sets a status bit in the cycle software writes 0 to that bit, the bit shall end 0: software's clear wins. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_09[`REQ_SLP_09`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A write to a pad's sleep mode while its status bit is 1 shall leave the pad as it is. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_10a[`REQ_SLP_10a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|After a write to a pad's sleep mode while its status bit is 1, the new mode shall act at the next sleep entry. (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_10b[`REQ_SLP_10b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

The four modes cover every sleep mode value and each is an equality, so together the mode checks
(forward and stable) also give the backward direction. One cover per mode row.

[%header,cols="1,2,1,1,3"]
|===
|Status bit |Entry, sleep enable 1 |Software clear |Bit next cycle |Decided by (one cover per row)
|0 |0 |0 or 1 |0 |_bit set only at entry_
|0 |1 |0 |1 |_bit set at entry_
|0 or 1 |1 |1 |0 |_clear wins_
|1 |0 or 1 |0 |1 |_bit holds until cleared_
|1 |0 |1 |0 |_clear releases_
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_tie high_ (base) |pad 26: enable 1, mode 1, select 81; a sleep entry |bit 1 from the cycle after the entry, pad (1, 1); _bit set at entry_, _tie high in sleep_
|_enable 0_ |pad 26's sleep enable at 0 |bit stays 0, pad follows select 81; _bit set only at entry_
|_keep driving_, _keep high-Z_ |mode 3 with (1, 1) in the set cycle; mode 3 with select 2 in the set cycle |(1, 1), (0, 0) while held; _keep holds_
|_one-cycle sleep pulse_ |`sleep_en_i` high for one cycle |bit 1 from the cycle after the entry, held after the fall; _bit set at entry_, _bit holds until cleared_
|_peripheral moves_ |output 78 toggles while held |pad unchanged; _tie high in sleep_
|_re-entry_, _enable written 0_ |a second entry, or the pad's sleep enable written 0, while held |bit stays 1, the set cycle unchanged; _bit holds until cleared_
|_mode write_ |pad 26 held in tie high (mode 1); mode 2 written; then a release and a new entry |(1, 1) stays while held; (0, 0) after the new entry; _mode write while held_, _high-Z in sleep_
|_release_ |`0xFBFFFFFF` to `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_0` |bit 26 is 0 in the next cycle, the others unchanged; _clear releases_
|_clear at entry_ |the release write in the cycle of the sleep entry |bit stays 0; _clear wins_
|_write of 1_ |`0xFFFFFFFF` to `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_0` while held |bit stays 1; _bit holds until cleared_
|_DIO pad_ |DIO 10 (IOR8), mode 0 |(0, 1) on DIO 10; _tie low in sleep_
|===

*Edge cases:* pads 31 and 32 (last bit of `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_0`, first of `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_1`), 46, DIO 0
and 15; an entry the
cycle after a release, a release the cycle after the set; `sleep_en_i` already 1 in the first
cycle after reset: no entry, the bit stays 0 (reading RD9; _bit set only at entry_). The bit
starts at 0 in every run, as software cannot write a `rw0c` bit to 1 ([RG]:74). +
*Never:* a bit rises without an entry with the enable at 1 (_bit set only at entry_; reached in
_enable 0_); a bit falls without a software clear or a reset, or a write of 1 clears it (_bit
holds until cleared_; reached in _failed clear_, _write of 1_); a held pad lets go when `sleep_en_i`
falls or its enable is written 0, or follows its peripheral or a later mode write (the mode checks, _mode write while held_; reached in _sleep over
select_, _mode write_); a kept value changes while held (_keep holds_; reached in _keep over select_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none; readings: sleep entry and its timing
(RD9), the sleep input runs on the pinmux's clock
(RD14), a held pad keeps what it took at sleep entry
(RD40).

[[tp_pad_attr]]
=== pad_attr: a pad gets exactly the attributes its register reads back

*Rule:* for every pad that is not an owned JTAG pad, asleep or awake, and for each field: the pad's attribute output
equals its read-back in that field in the same cycle, and that field of the read-back equals that field of the pad's
last attribute write if the pad library supports that field, else 0 ([TP] MioAttrO_A, DioAttrO_A; [REG] hjson:551-554;
[PG]:27-30; readings RD3, RD4, RD38). *Observed at:* `mio_attr_o`, `dio_attr_o`, the read-backs, the attribute writes on `tl_i`.

Checks and truth table, one cover per row (per pad type where the row names one):

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,3,1,5"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_pad_attr_01]]`CHK_PAD_ATTR_01` |pad gets read-back |both |the pad's attribute output equals its read-back in the same cycle, every field (REQ_ATTR_01a to REQ_ATTR_01j MIO, REQ_ATTR_02a to REQ_ATTR_02j DIO)
|[[chk_pad_attr_02]]`CHK_PAD_ATTR_02` |invert reads back |forward |every type, the last attribute write defined: the `invert` field of the read-back equals the `invert` field of the pad's last attribute write (REQ_ATTR_03)
|[[chk_pad_attr_03]]`CHK_PAD_ATTR_03` |open drain reads back |none |out of scope: chip level, the pad library's set (reading RD38; REQ_ATTR_04)
|[[chk_pad_attr_04]]`CHK_PAD_ATTR_04` |virtual open drain reads back |none |out of scope, as above (REQ_ATTR_05)

== Register locks, bus and alert

=== How it works

*Rule:* a closed attribute lock freezes what the pinmux stores (<<tp_regwen,regwen>>); requests
get TL-UL answers with correct codes, a failed one an error and no effect (<<tp_bus,bus>>) and
the fatal alert until reset, an alert test one event (<<tp_alert,alert>>); every other register
rule is csr_fpv's (xref:{tp}#tp_register_block[register_block]). Design doc:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#register_locks[Register locks],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#register_bus[Register block and bus].

[[tp_regwen]]
=== regwen: a closed attribute lock freezes the pad's attributes

*Rule:* for the attribute register of pad `p`, when the register's lock is 0 (closed) in a cycle and the pad is not an
owned JTAG pad in that cycle and the next, the pad's attribute output and its read-back keep their values into the next cycle
([REG] hjson:540-542, 644-646; [RG]:165). *Observed at:* `mio_attr_o`, `dio_attr_o`, the read-backs, the registers' locks.

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,2,1,6"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_regwen_01]]`CHK_REGWEN_01` |locked attribute holds |stable |the pad's attribute output unchanged while the lock is closed (REQ_LOCK_03a and REQ_LOCK_03b)
|[[chk_regwen_02]]`CHK_REGWEN_02` |locked read-back holds |stable |the pad's read-back unchanged while the lock is closed (REQ_LOCK_03a and REQ_LOCK_03b)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Locked attributes do not change (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_03a[`REQ_LOCK_03a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Locked attributes do not change (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_03b[`REQ_LOCK_03b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

The open direction is pad_attr's, the lock bit csr_fpv's (REQ_LOCK_01a to REQ_LOCK_01c).

[%header,cols="1,2,4,2"]
|===
|Lock |Write to the register |Expected |Decided by (one cover per row)
|1 |no write |unchanged |pad_attr
|1 |an accepted write to the register |the pad's read-back follows the pad's last attribute write |pad_attr
|0 |with or without a write |unchanged |both checks
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_locked write_ (base) |0 to `MIO_PAD_ATTR_REGWEN_26`, then `0x42` to `MIO_PAD_ATTR_26` |unchanged; both checks
|_other pad's lock_ |lock 25 closed, the write to pad 26 |lands; pad_attr _invert reads back_
|_reopen try_, _sleep while locked_ |1 to the lock after 0; entry and release on pad 26 |unchanged (the lock stays 0: csr_fpv); both checks
|_DIO pad_ |0 to `DIO_PAD_ATTR_REGWEN_10`, then a write to `DIO_PAD_ATTR_10` |unchanged; both checks
|_write, then lock_ |a write to pad 26, the lock closed by the next request |lands, then holds; pad_attr, both checks
|===

*Edge cases:* pad 30 locked at its reset value `0x4`; pads 0 and 46; DIO 0 and 15; the JTAG pads
with no TAP connected; the lock closed by the first request after reset. +
*Never:* a locked attribute changes on a write, a sleep entry or release, a select change or a
failed write (both checks; witness _locked attribute write_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none.

[[tp_bus]]
=== bus: every request is answered by the TL-UL rules, and a failed one changes nothing

*Rule:* the pinmux's port keeps the TL-UL device rules; every response carries the correct response code of
its opcode, size and error and the correct data code of its data; a failed request gets `d_error` 1 on its
response; a failed write is never an accepted write, so it changes no register: every register after a
failed write is decided here, after any other request by xref:{tp}#tp_register_block[register_block]
([TLUL]:107-109, 261-262, 299-312, 355-365, 380-381; [CIP]:216-224; reading RD12). *Observed at:*
`tl_i`, `tl_o`, every register's value (the pad's read-back for the attribute registers, the AON field for the registers of the AON fields).

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,3,1,5"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_bus_01]]`CHK_BUS_01` |device rules |forward |the TL-UL VIP's device rules on the pinmux's port: one response per request, with its source ID (REQ_BUS_01a to REQ_BUS_01c)
|[[chk_bus_02]]`CHK_BUS_02` |errors as the register checker predicts |both |indirect: csr_fpv's error answers for requests not failed (xref:{tp}#tp_register_block[register_block]); failed ones by _failed request errors_ (REQ_BUS_01a to REQ_BUS_01c)
|[[chk_bus_03]]`CHK_BUS_03` |response codes correct |forward |every response's codes are the correct response code and the correct data code (REQ_BUS_02a and REQ_BUS_02b)
|[[chk_bus_04]]`CHK_BUS_04` |failed request errors |forward |a failed request gets `d_error` 1 on its response (REQ_BUS_03)
|[[chk_bus_05]]`CHK_BUS_05` |failed write changes nothing |stable |every register software alone writes keeps its value, but for an AON field taking an earlier accepted write not yet landed (xref:{tp}#tp_wakeup_sync[wakeup_sync]); a field the hardware updates takes only that update (the status bit's next value, with no software clear of it) (REQ_BUS_04)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Answers by the TL-UL rules (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_01a[`REQ_BUS_01a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Answers by the TL-UL rules (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_01b[`REQ_BUS_01b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Answers by the TL-UL rules (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_01c[`REQ_BUS_01c`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Response integrity codes (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_02a[`REQ_BUS_02a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Response integrity codes (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_02b[`REQ_BUS_02b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|An error for a failed request (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_03[`REQ_BUS_03`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|No register change from a failed write (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_04[`REQ_BUS_04`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

[%header,cols="3,3,4"]
|===
|Condition |Expected |Decided by (one cover per row)
|a good request |gets the error answer csr_fpv predicts and lands |_errors as the register checker predicts_
|a bad command code, or a write with a bad data code |gets `d_error` 1 and changes nothing |_failed request errors_, _failed write changes nothing_
|a read whose only fault is its data code |no failed request (reading RD12) |_errors as the register checker predicts_, `alert` _no alert without a cause_
|every response |correct codes |_response codes correct_
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_good write_ (base) |81 to `MIO_OUTSEL_26` (offset `0x430`) |no error, lands; _errors as the register checker predicts_, _device rules_
|_bad command code_, _bad data code_ |one bit of either code flipped |error; `MIO_OUTSEL_26` and every other register unchanged; _failed request errors_, _failed write changes nothing_
|_bad read_ |a read of `MIO_OUTSEL_26` with a bad command code |error; _failed request errors_
|_bad attribute write_ |`0x1` to `MIO_PAD_ATTR_26`, bad code |pad 26's read-back unchanged; _failed write changes nothing_
|_bad lock, status or detector write_ |0 to `MIO_OUTSEL_REGWEN_26`; `0xFBFFFFFF` to `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_0` with pad 26 held; a detector register; each with a bad code |lock 1, bit 26 at 1, the AON field unchanged with no write in flight (also in V3); _failed write changes nothing_
|_read data code_ |a read of `MIO_PAD_ATTR_25` |codes correct over the data read; _response codes correct_
|===

*Edge cases:* a code wrong in one bit and in every bit; `ALERT_TEST` (offset `0x0`) and
`WKUP_CAUSE` (`0xA1C`, the last register); a failed write in the cycle an entry sets a status bit
(the set lands); back-to-back requests. +
*Never:* a failed request answered without error (_failed request errors_; witness _failed select
write_); a failed write changes a register (_failed write changes nothing_; witness _failed
clear_); a response with a wrong code (_response codes correct_; witness _read data code_); a
second or a missing response (_device rules_; witness _good write_).

*Run:* V1, integrity codes free; V3 for the registers of the AON fields in _failed write changes nothing_.
*Blocked by:* none; reading RD12, a read whose only fault is its data code included.

[[tp_alert]]
=== alert: the fatal alert follows a failed request or an alert test, and nothing else

*Rule:* the alert handler is the one of assumption A3; `AlertLat` is the bound of xref:{tp}#defs_pads[Pads, selection, sleep, attributes, locks and bus].
A failed request in a cycle is followed by an alert event within `AlertLat` cycles. While in the
fatal state, every cycle is followed by an alert event within `AlertLat` cycles, until reset. An
alert test in a cycle gives a test credit, used up within `AlertLat` cycles. A ping gives a ping
credit, an alert test a test credit. Each alert event uses up one credit: the ping credit first,
else the test credit, else the fatal state. A cause in an event's cycle keeps its credit. A ping
credit lapses `AlertLat` cycles after its ping. A ping meeting an alert gets its own handshake,
before or after it ([ALERT]:219-225), so a test and a ping take two events.
Sources: [REG] hjson:37-43; [COMP]:654, 695, 701; [ALERT]:129-169; `doc/registers.md:591-593`; reading RD13.
*Observed at:* `alert_tx_o`, `alert_rx_i`, `tl_i`, `tl_o`, the lock of `ALERT_TEST` (bit 31).

.Checks
[%header,cols="2,2,1,5"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_alert_01]]`CHK_ALERT_01` |failed request alerts |forward |a failed request in a cycle: an alert event within `AlertLat` cycles (REQ_BUS_05)
|[[chk_alert_02]]`CHK_ALERT_02` |fatal alert repeats |forward |in the fatal state: every cycle is followed by an alert event within `AlertLat` cycles, until reset (REQ_BUS_06)
|[[chk_alert_03]]`CHK_ALERT_03` |test sends an event |forward |an alert test in a cycle: its test credit used up within `AlertLat` cycles, so a test and a ping take two events (REQ_BUS_07)
|[[chk_alert_04]]`CHK_ALERT_04` |no alert without a cause |backward |an alert event only with the fatal state, a ping credit or a test credit; a write of bit 0 while the lock of `ALERT_TEST` is 0 sets no credit (REQ_BUS_08, REQ_BUS_09, and the "one" of REQ_BUS_07)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A failed request raises the alert (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_05[`REQ_BUS_05`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|It repeats until reset (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_06[`REQ_BUS_06`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|An alert test sends one event (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_07[`REQ_BUS_07`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|No test while testing is disabled (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_08[`REQ_BUS_08`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|No alert without a cause (xref:{reqs}#req_bus_09[`REQ_BUS_09`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

[%header,cols="3,2,4"]
|===
|Condition |Expected |Decided by (one cover per row)
|a failed request |events until reset |_failed request alerts_, _fatal alert repeats_
|a test write with testing enabled |one event |_test sends an event_, _no alert without a cause_
|a test write with testing disabled |no event |_no alert without a cause_
|a ping |one event allowed |_no alert without a cause_
|no cause |no event |_no alert without a cause_
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_bad command code_ (base) |a write with a bad command code in a cycle |an event, then a new one after every handshake until reset; _failed request alerts_, _fatal alert repeats_
|_test_ |`0x80000001` to `ALERT_TEST` |one event; _test sends an event_, _no alert without a cause_
|_test disabled_ |`0x0` to `ALERT_TEST` first, then `0x80000001` |no event; _no alert without a cause_
|_ping_ |a ping, no other cause |one event allowed; _no alert without a cause_
|_test during a ping answer_ |a test write while the ping's handshake runs |one more event; _test sends an event_
|_bad test write_ |`0x80000001` with a bad command code |no alert test; events until reset from the fatal state; _fatal alert repeats_
|===

*Edge cases:* `0x1` to `ALERT_TEST` (bit 31 written 0, bit 0 at 1): one test, one event (reading
RD13; _test sends an event_); two test writes before the first event (one credit, one event:
reading RD13; _no alert without a cause_); a test and a ping answered by one handshake (the test
credit left: _test sends an event_ fails); an event `AlertLat + 1` cycles after an unanswered ping
(its credit lapsed: _no alert without a cause_); a failed request in the cycle of a test write (one
event for both, then events until reset: reading RD13; _fatal alert repeats_); pings at the minimum
spacing of A3. +
*Never:* an alert with no failed request, test or ping, or a test while testing is disabled (_no
alert without a cause_; witness _test disabled_); the fatal alert stops before reset (_fatal alert
repeats_; witness _bad command code_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none; readings RD12, RD13, the test
write that also disables testing included.

'''

== Wakeup detectors

=== How it works

*Rule:* an enabled detector writes 1 to its cause bit on its mode's pattern; only software's
landed clear returns the bit to 0; the wakeup request (`pin_wkup_req_o`) follows any cause. Modes, registers, a worked example:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#wakeup_detectors[design doc, Wakeup detectors].
Three testpoints split the outputs: a cause set (<<tp_wakeup>>), the cause bit and the wakeup request
(<<tp_wakeup_cause>>), the AON fields (<<tp_wakeup_sync>>). Every rule holds between resets, with
scan mode not True (assumption A1), the mode unchanged while enabled (assumption A5), the other
detector fields written at any time (reading RD20) and
`sleep_en_i` free (reading RD17). Delays are bounds, never exact cycles (reading RD16),
except the register's one-cycle step (reading RD37).

'''

[[tp_wakeup]]
=== wakeup: a detector writes its cause bit on its pattern, and only then

*Rule:* for every detector, outside the start-up cycles (xref:{tp}#defs_wakeup[Wakeup and USB wakeup]); on the EG2 top only where `MIODIO`
and `PADSEL` name a constant, no pad, or a wakeup-capable pad (xref:{tp}#tp_wkup_capable[wkup_capable] decides
the rest, reading RD45):

* forward: a detection in a cycle with the enable held gives a cause set within `WkLat` cycles;
* backward: take a cause set of a bit at 0 that is not a set as a clear lands. It answers a pattern
  of the pad seen `k` late, for some `k`, with `EN` 1. No earlier such set has answered that pattern.
  A write of 1 to a bit at 1 is free (xref:{tp}#defs_wakeup[Wakeup and USB wakeup]);
* a cause set that is not a set as a clear lands gives the cause bit 1 in the next cycle (reading RD37; a set as a clear lands: <<tp_wakeup_cause>>).

*Observed at:* `mio_in_i`, `dio_in_i` (free), the AON fields, the cause sets, the cause bits. The pad select,
sampling and filter define the filtered pad: a wrong one fails an edge check or _no false cause_.

.Checks
[cols="2,2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_wakeup_01]]`CHK_WAKEUP_01` |posedge sets cause |forward |mode 0 (REQ_WKUP_06a and REQ_WKUP_06b, 11, 14)
|[[chk_wakeup_02]]`CHK_WAKEUP_02` |negedge sets cause |forward |mode 1 (REQ_WKUP_07a and REQ_WKUP_07b, 14)
|[[chk_wakeup_03]]`CHK_WAKEUP_03` |edge sets cause |forward |mode 2 (REQ_WKUP_08a and REQ_WKUP_08b, 14)
|[[chk_wakeup_04]]`CHK_WAKEUP_04` |timed high sets cause |forward |mode 3: a detection (the level 1 for `TH` + 1 cycles in a row) in a cycle with the enable held gives a cause set within `WkLat` cycles (REQ_WKUP_09; reading RD41)
|[[chk_wakeup_05]]`CHK_WAKEUP_05` |timed low sets cause |forward |mode 4: the same for the level 0 (REQ_WKUP_10; reading RD41)
|[[chk_wakeup_06]]`CHK_WAKEUP_06` |no false cause |backward |a cause set of a bit at 0 only on a pattern of an enabled detector (REQ_WKUP_12, 13, 15); in the timed modes never while the run length is below `TH` (REQ_WKUP_09, 10; reading RD41)
|[[chk_wakeup_07]]`CHK_WAKEUP_07` |set lands |forward |a cause set that is not a set as a clear lands gives the cause bit 1 in the next cycle (REQ_WKUP_14; reading RD37)
|===

|Mode |`EN` |Detected |Decided by
|0 (`MODE` 0, 5, 6, 7) |1 |a rise |_posedge sets cause_, _no false cause_
|1 |1 |a fall |_negedge sets cause_, _no false cause_
|2 |1 |a rise or a fall |_edge sets cause_, _no false cause_
|3, 4 |1 |the run length reaching `TH` + 1; a cause set never below `TH` |_timed high sets cause_, _timed low sets cause_, _no false cause_
|any |0, and the enable not near |nothing |_no false cause_
|===

.Cases. Base: detector 0, `EN` 1, `MODE` 0, `FILTER` 0, `MIODIO` 0, `PADSEL` 18 (IOB7), `sleep_en_i` 0, one rise far from any `EN` change
[cols="2,4,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varies |Expected |Decided by
|_rise detected_ |nothing |a cause set of detector 0 within `WkLat` cycles, its cause bit 1 the cycle after |_posedge sets cause_, _set lands_
|_one-sample pulse_ |the pad is 1 at one AON edge only |a cause set of detector 0 within `WkLat` cycles |_posedge sets cause_
|_fall in posedge mode_ |the pad falls instead |no cause set |_no false cause_
|_filter count_ |`FILTER` 1, the pad 1 for 3 samples; for 4 samples |no cause set; a cause set of detector 0 |_no false cause_; _posedge sets cause_
|_disabled_ |`EN` 0, the rise far from any `EN` change |no cause set |_no false cause_
|_enable on a steady pad_ |`FILTER` 1, the pad 1 for `SmpLat + 4` cycles, then `EN` rises |no cause set |_no false cause_ (REQ_WKUP_13a and REQ_WKUP_13b)
|_filter spans the enable_ |`FILTER` 1, the pad rises 2 samples before `EN` rises, so the filtered pad rises 1 cycle after |a cause set of detector 0 within `WkLat` cycles |_posedge sets cause_ (REQ_WKUP_13a and REQ_WKUP_13b)
|_edge at an enable change_ |the rise within `SmpLat` cycles before `EN` rises, or before it falls |a cause set allowed, none required |_no false cause_
|_pad select before the disable lands_ |no rise: the base pad held 0, MIO pad 17 held 1; software writes 0 to `WKUP_DETECTOR_EN_0`, then, while the disable is still crossing, 19 to `WKUP_DETECTOR_PADSEL_0`; `MODE` 0, also 2 |no cause set: the disable holds in the AON logic before a later write takes effect (reading RD18); `gap, raised with the designers`: the pad select does not cross to the AON clock (hjson:1119), and no spec orders it after a disable |no check: `gap, raised with the designers`, not built; the cover of this case looks for a cause set before the disable lands
|_pad select changed while enabled_ |MIO pad 17 held 1, the base pad held 0; software writes 19 to `WKUP_DETECTOR_PADSEL_0` |a cause set of detector 0 within `WkLat` cycles: the step of the watched value from 0 to 1 is a rise, not a false cause (reading RD20) |_posedge sets cause_, _no false cause_
|_pad select before the MIO or DIO choice lands_ |MIO pad 0 held 1, the base pad and DIO pad 2 held 0; software writes `0x10` to `WKUP_DETECTOR_0` (DIO, the mode kept), then, while it crosses, 2 to `WKUP_DETECTOR_PADSEL_0`: until `MIODIO` lands, the watched value is MIO pad 0, neither the old pad nor the new one |no cause set: the detector never watches a pad software did not choose (reading RD20); `gap, raised with the designers`: the pad select takes effect at once (hjson:1119), and the checks decode it with `MIODIO` as landed, so they follow the mix |no check: `gap, raised with the designers`, not built; the cover of this case looks for a cause set from MIO pad 0 before `MIODIO` lands
|_filter or threshold changed while enabled_ |while enabled: `FILTER` 0 to 1 two samples after the pad rises; or `MODE` 3, the level held 50 cycles, `TH` lowered from 100 to 10 |`gap, raised with the designers`: the checks read each field as landed, but no spec says what a filter turned on holds before 4 equal samples (the value it showed, or the last value held 4 samples), so the checks claim nothing until 4 equal samples; and with `TH` lowered to or below the level already held, _no false cause_ allows the cause set that reading RD20 asks for (the run length is at `TH` or above), but the run length never reaches the new `TH` + 1, so no check requires it |no check: `gap, raised with the designers`, not built; the cover of this case looks for a cause set within `WkLat` cycles of each change landing
|_asleep_ |`sleep_en_i` 1 |as the base |_posedge sets cause_
|===

*Edge cases*, decided by the edge checks and _no false cause_: `MIODIO` 0 with `PADSEL` 0, 1, 2,
48, 49, 63 watches 0, 1, MIO pad 0, MIO pad 46, 0, 0; `MIODIO` 1 with 0, 15, 16, 63 watches DIO pad
0, DIO pad 15, 0, 0; `MODE` 5 and 7; detector 7; a cause set `WkLat` cycles after its pattern (allowed);
`TH` 0, 1, 255 (reading RD41); while enabled (reading RD20): `TH` raised from 100 to 200 once a
level has held 5 cycles (a cause set once it has held 201 cycles, none before 200), `FILTER`
changed with the pad steady for 4 samples (no cause set), `FILTER` 1 to 0 two samples after a rise
(the filtered pad rises at once).
*Never:* a cause set with no pattern of an enabled detector near it, or from a disabled detector: _no
false cause_ (witness _detection, no write_, _disabled_); an enabled pattern with no cause set: the edge
checks (witness _rise detected_); a detection that depends on `sleep_en_i`: every check,
`sleep_en_i` free (witness _asleep_); a detector watching a pad software did not choose: no check,
`gap, raised with the designers` (witness _pad select before the MIO or DIO choice lands_).
*Run:* V1; V3 for the counts in AON cycles.
The mode unchanged while enabled (assumption A5) is read on the enable software last wrote, not
on the enable landed in the AON logic. *Blocked by:* the order of a pad select write after a
disable or a MIO or DIO choice, and a filter or threshold change while enabled,
for the three cases that name it;
the bounds (RD16), the timed count (RD41) and the start-up cycles (RD46).

'''

[[tp_wakeup_cause]]
=== wakeup_cause: a cause bit holds until software clears it, and the request follows the bits

*Observed at:* the hardware writes of the cause bits, the cause bits, the landed clears, `pin_wkup_req_o`.

*Rule:* for every detector, no hardware write of the cause bit writes 0 while the cause bit is 1 and no clear lands;
the cause bit falls only in the cycle after a landed clear or at `rst_aon_ni` (RD18); a set as a clear lands
gives the cause bit 0 in the next cycle: software's clear wins, per bit ([REG] hjson:1150-1151;
[RG]:810, 815, 884-900; reading RD37). Any cause rising gives the wakeup request 1 within `ReqLat` cycles, and
any cause 1 for `ReqLat + 1` cycles in a row gives the wakeup request 1; any cause 0 for `ReqLat + 1` cycles in
a row gives the wakeup request 0. Precedence on the cause bit: a cause set without a landed clear is
<<tp_wakeup>>'s _set lands_; a landed clear without a cause set is <<tp_wakeup_sync>>'s _landed clear clears
cause_; both in one cycle: _set and clear together_ (witnesses _set then clear_, _set as clear lands_,
_detection, no write_).

.Checks
[cols="2,2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_wakeup_cause_01]]`CHK_WAKEUP_CAUSE_01` |hardware only sets cause |stable |no hardware write of the cause bit writes 0 while the cause bit is 1 and no clear lands (REQ_WKUP_16)
|[[chk_wakeup_cause_02]]`CHK_WAKEUP_CAUSE_02` |cause holds until cleared |stable |the cause bit falls only after a landed clear or at `rst_aon_ni` (REQ_WKUP_16)
|[[chk_wakeup_cause_03]]`CHK_WAKEUP_CAUSE_03` |set and clear together |forward |a set as a clear lands gives the cause bit 0 in the next cycle: the clear wins (REQ_WKUP_17; reading RD37)
|[[chk_wakeup_cause_04]]`CHK_WAKEUP_CAUSE_04` |request follows cause |forward |any cause rising, or 1 for `ReqLat + 1` cycles in a row, gives the wakeup request 1 (REQ_WKUP_18a and REQ_WKUP_18b)
|[[chk_wakeup_cause_05]]`CHK_WAKEUP_CAUSE_05` |no request without cause |backward |any cause 0 for `ReqLat + 1` cycles in a row gives the wakeup request 0 (REQ_WKUP_18a and REQ_WKUP_18b)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The bit holds (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_16[`REQ_WKUP_16`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A set as a clear lands (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_17[`REQ_WKUP_17`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The request (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_18a[`REQ_WKUP_18a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The request (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_18b[`REQ_WKUP_18b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

.Cases. Base: the cause bit of detector 0 set by a detection, the other bits 0. The last three rows are the truth table of the wakeup request: any cause held 1, held 0, 1 for one cycle
[cols="2,4,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varies |Expected |Decided by
|_bit holds_ |`EN`, `MODE` and the pad change after the set, a second rise included; or software writes 1 to bit 0 |the cause bit of detector 0 stays 1 |_cause holds until cleared_, _hardware only sets cause_
|_AON reset_ |`rst_aon_ni` low |the cause bit of detector 0 is 0 |indirect: csr_fpv reset values
|_set as clear lands_ |a second rise sets bit 0 in the cycle a clear of it lands |the cause bit of detector 0 is 0 the cycle after; wakeup _set lands_ and wakeup_sync _landed clear clears cause_ make no claim |_set and clear together_
|_one of two cleared_ |cause bits 0 and 3 set, bit 0 cleared |the wakeup request stays 1 |_request follows cause_
|_last bit cleared_ |bit 0 cleared |the wakeup request 0 within `ReqLat` cycles |_no request without cause_
|_one-cycle cause_ |a clear lands in the cycle after the set lands |the wakeup request 1 at least once within `ReqLat` cycles |_request follows cause_
|===

*Edge cases:* detector 7's bit (_cause holds until cleared_, _request follows cause_); all eight bits 1
(_request follows cause_); a `WKUP_CAUSE` write of `0xFE` (clears bit 0 only) and of `0x00`, each also as
detector 1 sets: bit 1 ends 1 after `0xFE` (wakeup _set lands_), 0 after `0x00` (_set and clear together_).
*Never:* hardware clears a cause bit: _hardware only sets cause_, _cause holds until cleared_
(witness _set then clear_); a set wins over a clear landing in its cycle: _set and clear together_
(witness _set as clear lands_); the wakeup request 1 while every cause bit has been 0 for `ReqLat + 1`
cycles in a row: _no request without cause_ (witness _last bit cleared_); the wakeup request 0 while
any cause has been 1 for `ReqLat + 1` cycles in a row: _request follows cause_ (witness _one of two cleared_).
*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none; readings RD16, RD19.

'''

[[tp_wakeup_sync]]
=== wakeup_sync: every write to the AON fields and every clear reaches the AON logic in bounded time

*Observed at:* the AON field writes and
the software clears of the cause bit on `tl_i`; the AON fields, the landed clears, the cause bits.

*Rule:* for every detector and AON field `f` (`EN`, `MODE`, `FILTER`, `MIODIO`, `TH`), an AON field write of `v` to `f`
in a cycle gives `f` the value `v` within `AonLat` cycles, until the next AON field write to `f` lands; `f` changes only to the
value of an AON field write not yet landed; a software clear of the cause bit lands within `AonLat` cycles, and a landed
clear follows only a software clear not yet landed; a landed clear, seen at the AON-side write, that is not a set as a
clear lands gives the cause bit 0 in the next cycle (reading RD37). A write
after a write to the same register waits for it (hjson:983-984): at most one per field is in
flight. A write to another field of the detector may be accepted while one crosses; it lands in
the same AON cycle as the earlier write or after it, never before (reading RD18).

.Checks
[cols="2,2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_01]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_01` |write lands |forward |field `f` holds `v` within `AonLat` cycles of an AON field write of `v`, until the next write lands (REQ_WKUP_19a to REQ_WKUP_19d)
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_02]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_02` |no change without a write |backward |field `f` changes only to the value of an AON field write not yet landed (REQ_WKUP_19a to REQ_WKUP_19d)
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_03]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_03` |clear lands |forward |a software clear of the cause bit lands within `AonLat` cycles (REQ_WKUP_19a to REQ_WKUP_19d)
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_04]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_04` |no clear without a write |backward |a clear lands only after a software clear of the cause bit not yet landed (REQ_WKUP_19a to REQ_WKUP_19d)
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_05]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_05` |landed clear clears cause |forward |the cause bit is 0 in the next cycle after a landed clear, unless it is a set as a clear lands (REQ_WKUP_19a to REQ_WKUP_19d; reading RD37)
|[[chk_wakeup_sync_06]]`CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_06` |writes land in order |forward |an AON field write accepted while a write to another field of the same detector is crossing lands in the same AON cycle as that write or after it (REQ_WKUP_20a and REQ_WKUP_20b; reading RD18)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The crossing to the AON clock (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_19a[`REQ_WKUP_19a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The crossing to the AON clock (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_19b[`REQ_WKUP_19b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The crossing to the AON clock (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_19c[`REQ_WKUP_19c`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The crossing to the AON clock (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_19d[`REQ_WKUP_19d`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The order of writes (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_20a[`REQ_WKUP_20a`]) |_writes land in order_ (<<chk_wakeup_sync_06,CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_06>>) |it compares the AON cycles in which a configuration write and a later enable write land; an enable that holds before the configuration fails it
|The order of writes (xref:{reqs}#req_wkup_20b[`REQ_WKUP_20b`]) |_writes land in order_ (<<chk_wakeup_sync_06,CHK_WAKEUP_SYNC_06>>) |the same for a threshold write and a later enable write; an enable that holds before the threshold fails it
|===

.Cases. Base: `EN_0` 0, software writes `0x0C` to `WKUP_DETECTOR_0`, then 1 to `EN_0`
[cols="2,4,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varies |Expected |Decided by
|_config lands_ |nothing |the AON fields of `WKUP_DETECTOR_0` hold `0x0C` within `AonLat` |_write lands_
|_enable lands_ |nothing |`EN` 1 within `AonLat` |_write lands_
|_threshold lands_ |255 written to `CNT_TH_0` |`TH` 255 |_write lands_
|_write at the bound_ |landing `AonLat` cycles after |allowed |_write lands_
|_write while a write to another field is crossing_ |the write of 1 to `EN_0` accepted while the write of `0x0C` still crosses |each lands within `AonLat`; `EN` holds 1 no earlier than the fields hold `0x0C` (reading RD18) |_write lands_, _writes land in order_
|_locked write_ |`WKUP_DETECTOR_REGWEN_0` 0 first |not taken, no change |_no change without a write_
|_clear lands_ |`0x00` written to `WKUP_CAUSE` with bit 0 at 1 |bit 0 at 0 within `AonLat + 1` |_clear lands_, _landed clear clears cause_
|_write of 1_ |`0x01` written to `WKUP_CAUSE` with bit 0 at 1 |no landed clear, the bit stays 1 |_no clear without a write_
|===

*Edge cases:* detector 7; `TH` 0, 255; `MODE` 7; a write of the value already held (_write lands_);
two writes landing in one AON cycle (_writes land in order_, allowed). *Never:* an AON
field changes with no AON field write not yet landed, or a clear lands with no software clear of the cause bit
not yet landed: the two backward checks (witness _locked write_,
_write of 1_); a field written later holding its value before a field written earlier: _writes
land in order_ (witness _write while a write to another field is crossing_).
*Run:* V1, V3 (the real crossing ratio). *Blocked by:* the bound `AonLat` and the order of writes
to two registers (RD18).

'''

== USB wakeup wiring

=== How it works

*Rule:* each port of usbdev's wakeup module carries the pinmux signal of the same role, unchanged,
on the AON clock and reset; what the module does is usbdev's (xref:{tp}#tp_usb_module[usb_module]). Ports and roles:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#usb_wakeup[design doc, USB wakeup].

'''

[[tp_usb_conn]]
=== usb_conn: every module port carries the pinmux signal of the same role

*Rule:* in every cycle, each pair below is equal ([ToO]:46-47; [IF]:31-41; [TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:1234-1242).
An equality decides both directions; a value on the wrong wire fails it whatever the value, so no
legal or stable check is needed. *Observed at:* the pinmux ports and the module's ports; the
module's outputs may be cut and free (TB architecture doc).

.Checks
[cols="2,2,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Equal pair |Req
|[[chk_usb_conn_01]]`CHK_USB_CONN_01` |D+ pull-up enable in |the module's `usbdev_dppullup_en_i` port and `usbdev_dppullup_en` |01
|[[chk_usb_conn_02]]`CHK_USB_CONN_02` |D- pull-up enable in |the same for D- |01
|[[chk_usb_conn_03]]`CHK_USB_CONN_03` |suspend request in |the module's suspend request port and `usbdev_suspend_req` |01
|[[chk_usb_conn_04]]`CHK_USB_CONN_04` |wake acknowledge in |the module's wake acknowledge port and `usbdev_wake_ack` |01
|[[chk_usb_conn_05]]`CHK_USB_CONN_05` |D+ pull-up enable out |`usb_dppullup_en` and the module's `usb_dppullup_en_o` port |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_06]]`CHK_USB_CONN_06` |D- pull-up enable out |the same for D- |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_07]]`CHK_USB_CONN_07` |bus not idle out |`usbdev_bus_not_idle` and the module's port of the resume event |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_08]]`CHK_USB_CONN_08` |bus reset out |`usbdev_bus_reset` and the module's port of the bus reset event |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_09]]`CHK_USB_CONN_09` |sense lost out |`usbdev_sense_lost` and the module's port of the VBUS lost event |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_10]]`CHK_USB_CONN_10` |active out |`usbdev_wake_detect_active` and the module's `wake_detect_active_aon_o` port |02
|[[chk_usb_conn_11]]`CHK_USB_CONN_11` |wake request out |`usb_wkup_req` and the module's `wake_req_aon_o` port (RD21) |03

which equal clocks cannot tell apart. The reset check cannot tell `rst_aon_ni` from `rst_ni`: both are held released

'''

== Straps and TAPs

=== How it works

*Rule:* when the TAP straps name a TAP and its gate is open (the TAP is connected), the TAP's request equals the JTAG
pads as a request in the same cycle; while it is cut, the TAP's request is 0 (background:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#strap_sampling[strap sampling],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#latched_debug_enable[latched debug enable],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection],
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#dft_straps[DFT straps]).

[%header,cols="3,2"]
|===
|Output |Decided by
|The TAP's request of each of the three TAPs |<<tp_jtag>>
|The TAP straps, at the sampled straps (TB unit boundary) |<<tp_strap>>
|The latched debug enable (`pinmux_hw_debug_en_o`), which `jtag` reads as the RISC-V TAP's gate |<<tp_latch>>
|`dft_strap_test_o` |<<tp_dft_strap>>
|MIO 35 to 39 while the JTAG pads are taken (a TAP is connected) |<<tp_jtag_pad>>
|===

For the TAP straps, the TAP ports follow through the two checks of `jtag`, so the two cannot answer differently.

'''

[[tp_strap]]
=== strap: the TAP straps sample as the life cycle allows and hold otherwise

*Rule:* in full reset both TAP straps are 0. Out of full reset, a bit that samples in a cycle shows its strap pad's
`mio_in_i` value of that cycle in the next cycle: strap 0 (MIO pad 30) at a strap pulse or with every-cycle sampling;
strap 1 (MIO pad 27) with every-cycle sampling, or at a strap pulse with `lc_hw_debug_en_i` steadily On. A bit with
every-cycle sampling ruled out and no strap pulse sampling it keeps its value; otherwise it is unknown. With every-cycle
sampling, strap 1 takes its pad at a strap pulse whatever the debug enable: every-cycle sampling (REQ_STRAP_03) takes
precedence over strap 1 at the strap pulse (REQ_STRAP_02a and REQ_STRAP_02b, reading RD22). With the TAP hold at 1, every-cycle sampling
is ruled out and the strap pulse rule for strap 1 (REQ_STRAP_02a and REQ_STRAP_02b) keeps strap 1 (REQ_STRAP_04). `rst_ni`, `rst_aon_ni` and `strap_en_override_i` are not inputs ([ToO]:117-127, 139, 151;
[IF]:29). Strap 1 follows the live debug enable at the strap pulse, its row's [ToO] source. *Observed at:* the sampled straps (TB unit boundary), the TAP ports by composition through `jtag`
_connected TAP gets the pads_ and _cut TAP gets zero_.

.Checks
[cols="2,2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_strap_01]]`CHK_STRAP_01` |pulse samples the straps |forward |strap 0 takes its pad at every strap pulse; strap 1 takes its pad with `lc_hw_debug_en_i` steadily On, and is kept with it steadily Off and every-cycle sampling ruled out (REQ_STRAP_01, 02)
|[[chk_strap_02]]`CHK_STRAP_02` |straps follow the pads |forward |with every-cycle sampling, both straps take the pads one cycle late (REQ_STRAP_03)
|[[chk_strap_03]]`CHK_STRAP_03` |straps hold |stable |no strap pulse and every-cycle sampling ruled out: no change, through any override value (REQ_STRAP_04, 05, 08)
|[[chk_strap_04]]`CHK_STRAP_04` |unsampled strap reads 0 |forward |the TAP straps are 00 from a full reset until a sample (REQ_STRAP_06)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Strap 0 at the strap pulse (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_01[`REQ_STRAP_01`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Strap 1 at the strap pulse (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_02a[`REQ_STRAP_02a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Strap 1 at the strap pulse (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_02b[`REQ_STRAP_02b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Every-cycle sampling in the test states (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_03[`REQ_STRAP_03`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Paused by the TAP hold (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_04[`REQ_STRAP_04`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Held otherwise (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_05[`REQ_STRAP_05`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|0 until sampled (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_06[`REQ_STRAP_06`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Kept by an NDM reset (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_07[`REQ_STRAP_07`]) |none |Not covered by formal: reset behaviour is out of scope
|The override ignored (xref:{reqs}#req_strap_08[`REQ_STRAP_08`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

[cols="1,2,2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Row: strap pulse |Every-cycle sampling |Debug enable |TAP straps, next cycle |Decided by
|Row 1: 1 |any |steadily On |pads |_pulse samples the straps_
|Row 2: 1 |ruled out |steadily Off |strap 0 takes pad 30, strap 1 kept |_pulse samples the straps_
|Row 3: 1 |yes |in its window |pads |_straps follow the pads_
|Row 4: 1 |yes |steadily Off |pads: every-cycle sampling wins (REQ_STRAP_03) |_straps follow the pads_
|Row 5: 1 |ruled out; or `lc_dft_en_i` in its window, hold 0 |in its window, with it ruled out; steadily Off or in its window, with `lc_dft_en_i` in its window |strap 0 takes pad 30, strap 1 unknown |_pulse samples the straps_ (strap 0)
|Row 6: 0 |yes |any |pads |_straps follow the pads_
|Row 7: 0 |ruled out |any |kept |_straps hold_
|Row 8: 0 |`lc_dft_en_i` in its window, hold 0 |any |unknown |none (RD23)
|Row 9: in full reset |any |any |00 |_unsampled strap reads 0_
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_DEV boot_ (base) |DEV (debug On, test Off held), IOC8 at 1, IOC5 at 0, strap pulse in cycle 5 |TAP straps 01 from 6, the LC TAP connected; _pulse samples the straps_
|_PROD boot_ |debug enable Off, IOC5 at 1 |01, strap 1 kept; _pulse samples the straps_
|_GPIO use after boot_ |IOC5 toggles |kept; _straps hold_
|_tester switches_ |test enable On held, IOC5 rises in 20 |11 from 21; _straps follow the pads_
|_one-cycle pad pulse_ |IOC8 high in 20 only |strap 0 at 1 in 21 only; _straps follow the pads_
|_hold pauses_ |TAP hold at 1 from 19 |kept; _straps hold_
|_one-cycle test enable_ |DEV, On in 20 only |unknown after 21, 22, held from 23; _straps hold_
|_override_ |0 to 1 |kept; _straps hold_
|===

*Edge cases:* the strap pulse in the first cycle out of full reset (both enables count as steadily Off: row 2) and in
the second (in its window: row 5); the strap pulse as the TAP hold rises; a pad change in the pulse cycle and the next
(the pulse cycle's value counts); the TAP hold falling with the test enable On. Witness of row 4: strap pulse, test
enable On held, debug enable Off held, IOC5 at 1, strap 1 at 0: 1 by _straps follow the pads_; _pulse samples the
straps_ is silent, its kept half needing every-cycle sampling ruled out.

*Never:* a TAP strap changes with no strap pulse and every-cycle sampling ruled out (_straps hold_; witness _straps
kept_; row 8, `lc_dft_en_i` in its window, is free); a PROD chip samples strap 1 (_pulse samples the straps_; witness
_PROD boot_); the override changes a strap (_straps hold_; witness _override_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* RD22, RD23, RD25.

'''

[[tp_dft_strap]]
=== dft_strap: the DFT straps are sampled once at boot in the test states and held

*Rule:* the DFT strap output (`dft_strap_test_o`) is (valid, straps). A strap pulse with `lc_dft_en_i` steadily On sets
it, in the next cycle, to valid 1 with the strap pads of the pulse cycle (`mio_in_i[42]`, `mio_in_i[40]`); once valid,
it keeps its value into the next cycle unless that cycle is in full reset; it is 0 while no strap pulse since the last
full reset came with `lc_dft_en_i` not steadily Off ([ToO]:121, 125; [IF]:25; [TP] `DftStrapTestOValidStable_A`,
`DftStrapTestOStrapStable_A`, hjson:784-790; [CHIP]:214-215). Sampled once at boot, the [ToO] source. *Observed at:* `dft_strap_test_o`.

.Checks

|[[chk_dft_strap_02]]`CHK_DFT_STRAP_02` |DFT straps held |stable |once valid, no change until a full reset (REQ_DFT_02a and REQ_DFT_02b)
|[[chk_dft_strap_03]]`CHK_DFT_STRAP_03` |zero until sampled |backward |all 0 before a qualifying strap pulse, whatever the strap pads (REQ_DFT_03)
|===

sampled_; witness _PROD boot_); a sampled value changing before a full reset (_DFT straps held_; witness _pads change
after boot_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* RD24, RD25.

'''

[[tp_latch]]
=== latch: the debug enable is taken at boot, cleared by life cycle, kept otherwise

*Rule:* in full reset the latched debug enable is Off. Out of full reset, in the next cycle: after a life cycle clear it
is Off; else after a strap pulse it is On if `lc_hw_debug_en_i` is steadily On and every clear is steadily Off, Off if
`lc_hw_debug_en_i` is steadily Off; else, with every clear steadily Off, it keeps its value. It is On or Off in every
cycle ([ToO]:151-159; [IF]:21; [LC] `lc_ctrl.hjson`:353-355, 367, `interfaces.md`:171-172; RD24, RD26). `rst_ni` and
`rst_aon_ni` are not inputs. *Observed at:* `pinmux_hw_debug_en_o`.

|[[chk_latch_03]]`CHK_LATCH_03` |On only at a pulse |backward |the latched debug enable rises to On only after a strap pulse with `lc_hw_debug_en_i` not steadily Off and not a life cycle clear, a clear input in its window included (REQ_DBG_01a and REQ_DBG_01b, 08)
|[[chk_latch_04]]`CHK_LATCH_04` |clear turns Off |forward |any life cycle clear, one in the pulse cycle included, gives Off (REQ_DBG_03 to 05, 09)
|[[chk_latch_05]]`CHK_LATCH_05` |latch holds |stable |no strap pulse and every clear steadily Off: no change (REQ_DBG_02, 06)
|[[chk_latch_06]]`CHK_LATCH_06` |output On or Off |legal |never another value (REQ_DBG_07a and REQ_DBG_07b)
|===

[[tp_jtag]]
=== jtag: the TAP the straps ask for gets the pads only while life cycle allows it

*Rule:* for every TAP: while it is connected, the TAP's request equals the JTAG pads as a request in the same cycle, but
in scan mode the `trst_n` field of the TAP's request equals `rst_ni` in that cycle; while it is cut and not in scan
mode, the TAP's request is 0 ([ToO]:129-137, 154, 157; [IF]:21; [TP] `LcJtagWoScanmode_A`, `LcJtagWScanmode_A`,
`LcJtagODefault_A` and their RV and DFT twins, hjson:616-710). The RISC-V TAP's gate is the latched debug enable, the
[ToO] and [IF] source. *Observed at:* `lc_jtag_o`, `rv_jtag_o`, `dft_jtag_o`.

.Checks

|[[chk_jtag_02]]`CHK_JTAG_02` |cut TAP gets zero |backward |no request without the TAP straps naming the TAP and its gate open (REQ_TAP_04)
|[[chk_jtag_03]]`CHK_JTAG_03` |only On opens |legal |indirect, no property of its own: the strict test in every gate, decided over the 15 other values by _cut TAP gets zero_, `strap` _pulse samples the straps_ and `latch` _pulse samples debug enable_ (REQ_TAP_05)
|[[chk_jtag_04]]`CHK_JTAG_04` |scan TRST follows reset |forward |in scan mode the `trst_n` field of a connected TAP's request is `rst_ni` (REQ_TAP_13; V6)
|===

|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_LC TAP_ (base) |TEST_UNLOCKED0, both enables On held, the latched debug enable On, TAP straps 01 |`lc_jtag_o` equals the JTAG pads as a request, the others 0; both checks
|_switch to DFT_ |TAP straps 11 from 21 |`dft_jtag_o` equals the JTAG pads as a request, `lc_jtag_o` 0 from 21; both checks
|_DEV asks DFT_ |test enable Off held |all 0; _cut TAP gets zero_
|_latch cleared_ |TAP straps 10, the latched debug enable Off from 33 |`rv_jtag_o` 0 from 33; _cut TAP gets zero_
|_test enable drops_ |in 30 |free in 31, 0 from 32; _cut TAP gets zero_

|_corrupt test enable_ |4'b1011 held |0; _cut TAP gets zero_

*Edge cases:* all 16 values of `lc_dft_en_i` held with TAP straps 11 (one opens); the TAP straps and a gate changing in
one cycle; a test enable step or pulse seen on TCK and TRST_N, which the RTL gates a cycle later than TMS and TDI
