the latched debug enable Off (_cut TAP gets zero_; witness _transition clear_); a field of the TAP's request other than
the pad's (_connected TAP gets the pads_; witness _one-cycle TCK pulse_).

*Run:* V1 (A1); V6 for scan mode. *Blocked by:* RD23, RD27; the timing reading (RD23) includes the gates' same-cycle delay from the TAP straps and the latched debug enable.

'''

[[tp_jtag_pad]]
=== jtag_pad: while a TAP is connected, the five JTAG pads belong to it

*Rule:* while a TAP is connected and scan mode is not True, awake or asleep (reading RD44): MIO pad 36 drives the `tdo` and `tdo_oe` of the
connected TAP's response as its data and enable, in the same cycle; MIO 35, 37, 38 and 39 have `mio_oe_o` 0; MIO
35 to 39 have every field of the attribute output 0. In every cycle the read-back of each of the five pads changes only
by a software write ([ToO]:144-145; [TP] `LcJtagI_A`, `RvJtagI_A`, `DftJtagI_A`, hjson:751-772; RD28). The pad's
drive, the pad's attribute output and the read-back are the pad terms (xref:{tp}#defs_pads[Pads, selection, sleep, attributes, locks and bus]). *Observed at:* `mio_out_o[36]`;
`mio_oe_o`, `mio_attr_o` of MIO 35 to 39; their read-backs.

.Checks
[cols="2,2,1,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts
|[[chk_jtag_pad_01]]`CHK_JTAG_PAD_01` |JTAG pad in sleep mode |forward |a JTAG pad asleep (status bit 1) while a TAP is connected: the checks below hold as awake, so sleep does not cut the TAP (REQ_TAP_11; reading RD44)
|[[chk_jtag_pad_02]]`CHK_JTAG_PAD_02` |TDO pad drives the TAP |forward |MIO pad 36 drives the `tdo` and `tdo_oe` of the connected TAP's response (REQ_TAP_06a and REQ_TAP_06b)
|[[chk_jtag_pad_03]]`CHK_JTAG_PAD_03` |input pads not driven |forward |output enable 0 on MIO 35, 37, 38, 39 (REQ_TAP_07)
|[[chk_jtag_pad_04]]`CHK_JTAG_PAD_04` |JTAG attributes zero |forward |every field of the attribute output 0 on MIO 35 to 39 (REQ_TAP_08)
|[[chk_jtag_pad_05]]`CHK_JTAG_PAD_05` |attribute registers untouched |stable |connecting or cutting a TAP leaves the five registers (REQ_TAP_09)
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|TDO drives the TAP's response (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_06a[`REQ_TAP_06a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|TDO drives the TAP's response (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_06b[`REQ_TAP_06b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|The input pads not driven (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_07[`REQ_TAP_07`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Attributes all 0 (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_08[`REQ_TAP_08`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|Registers unchanged (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_09[`REQ_TAP_09`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|What a peripheral reads (REQ_TAP_10: out of scope, reading RD43), sleep against a TAP (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_11[`REQ_TAP_11`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

The backward direction, the pads' own rules while the JTAG pads are free (every TAP cut), is the pad testpoints'.

[%header,cols="3,3"]
|===
|Truth table row |Decided by
|The JTAG pads taken |this testpoint
|The JTAG pads free |the pad testpoints
|In between |none
|Sleep active with a TAP connected |the same checks: reading RD44
|===

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Case |Varied from the base |Expected; decided by
|_LC TAP_ (base) |TAP straps 01, software set pull-up and inversion on MIO 38 and an output on MIO 35, `tdo` 1 with `tdo_oe` 1 |MIO pad 36 drives 1, MIO 35 not driven, the attribute output of MIO 38 0, register kept; all four checks
|_RV or DFT TAP_ |connected |same
|_TDO enable low_ |as named |`mio_oe_o[36]` 0
|_TAP cut_ |DEV with TAP straps 11 |the pad testpoints decide
|_connect and release_ |TAP straps 01 then 00, no write |_attribute registers untouched_
|_one-cycle TDO pulse_ |as named |pad 36 that cycle only
|_sleep on a JTAG pad_ |sleep enable 1, a sleep entry with a TAP connected |_JTAG pad in sleep mode_
|===

*Edge cases:* a software write to a JTAG pad's attribute register while a TAP is connected (it lands, the pad's
attribute output stays 0); a pad in sleep mode while a TAP is connected (the forward checks hold: reading RD44). *Never:* a
JTAG input pad driven while a TAP is connected, or TDO cut by sleep (_input pads not driven_, _TDO pad drives the TAP_; witness _straps ask DFT_, _sleep on a JTAG pad_); a non-zero field of
a JTAG pad's attribute output while a TAP is connected (_JTAG attributes zero_; witness _owned pad_); a register changed
by the TAP (_attribute registers untouched_; witness _connect and release_).

*Run:* V1. *Blocked by:* none; RD28, RD43, RD44.

'''

'''

== Design-wide and end to end

Requirements closed by composition or by another plan, the consistency witnesses between
testpoints and the environment's witness covers.

[[definitions]]
=== Terms

Every term a rule uses, in plain words, with its source and Earlgrey's values (EG2's in
defs eg2; xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#earlgrey_instance[Earlgrey instance]).
Time is in `clk_i` cycles, the wakeup detectors' in `clk_aon_i` cycles; "in the next cycle" is the
one after the cycle named, "within N cycles" that cycle or one of the N after it. Every rule holds
between two resets, with scan mode not True (assumption A1) except in
run V6; register values are the register block's, its own rules csr_fpv's (tp register block).
One term per concept in every testpoint. Worked numbers, counts: `python3 -c` on the Source formulas.

[[defs_pads]]
==== Pads, selection, sleep, attributes, locks and bus

[%header,cols="2,7,3"]
|===
|Term |Meaning |Source
|MIO pad, DIO pad, input, output |MIO pads 0 to 46 (`NMio` 47); DIO pads 0 to 15 (`NDio` 16); MIO peripheral inputs 0 to 96 (`NIn` 97); MIO peripheral outputs 0 to 105 (`NOut` 106). Where a register or port name needs the number, it is `p`, `d`, `n`, `k` |[REG] hjson:335-395; design doc, index letters
|The pad's type |BidirStd: MIO 0-5, 9-17, 22-31, 35-42 (33 pads), DIO 2-9, 14, 15. BidirOd: MIO 6-8, 18-21, 32-34, 43-46 (14 pads), DIO 10, 11. InputStd: DIO 12, 13. DualBidirTol: DIO 0, 1 |[TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson:1532-1690`; `33 + 14 = 47`
|An owned JTAG pad |A JTAG pad, MIO 35 to 39 (IOR0 to IOR4), in a cycle the JTAG pads are not free (<<defs_tap>>): a TAP is connected, or a TAP strap bit or the gate of the TAP the straps name is unknown or in its window |[TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson:1784-1793`; readings RD28, RD23; xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection]
|The input select, the selected input value |The input select of input `n` is `MIO_PERIPH_INSEL_n`, 6 bits, 0 to 63. The selected input value, what the input must read, by select: 0 reads 0; 1 reads 1; 2 to 48 (`1 + NMio`) read MIO pad number select minus 2 on `mio_in_i`; 49 (`2 + NMio`) to 63 read 0 |[REG] hjson:457-470; [TP] InSelOOB_A; reading RD2
|The pad's drive |The pair (`mio_out_o[p]`, `mio_oe_o[p]`), written (out, oe); for DIO pad `d`, (`dio_out_o[d]`, `dio_oe_o[d]`) |[IF]:84-99
|The output select, the selected drive |The output select of pad `p` is `MIO_OUTSEL_p`, 7 bits, 0 to 127. The selected drive, what the pad must drive, by select: 0 drives (0, 1); 1 drives (1, 1); 2 drives (0, 0); 3 to 108 (`2 + NOut`) drive output `k`, select minus 3, as (`periph_to_mio_i[k]`, `periph_to_mio_oe_i[k]`); 109 (`3 + NOut`) to 127 drive (0, 0). A DIO pad's selected drive is its own peripheral: (`periph_to_dio_i[d]`, `periph_to_dio_oe_i[d]`) |[REG] hjson:502-515; [ToO]:74; [TP] OutSel2_A, OutSelOOB_A, DOutSelN_A; reading RD2
|Select edges |Input: 0, 1, 2 (pad 0), 48 (pad 46), 49 (first naming no pad), 63. Output: 0, 1, 2, 3 (output 0), 108 (output 105), 109 (first naming no output), 127. Worked: UART0 receive (input 78) on IOC3 (pad 25) is select 27; UART0 transmit (output 78) on IOC4 (pad 26) is select 81 |`2 + 46`, `2 + 47`, `3 + 105`, `3 + 106`, `2 + 25`, `3 + 78`
|A sleep entry |A cycle in which `sleep_en_i` is 1 and was 0 in the cycle before, both cycles after the last reset; `sleep_en_i` changes only on `clk_i` edges (assumption A4) |[TP] "At posedge of sleep_en_i"; readings RD9, RD14
|The pad's sleep enable, its sleep mode |The pad's sleep enable (1 bit) and sleep mode (2 bits: 0 tie low, 1 tie high, 2 high-Z, 3 keep), `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_EN_p`, `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_MODE_p`; DIO pads the `DIO_` twins |[REG] hjson:735-955 (the enable: 904-905; its lock: 782, 894)
|The pad's sleep status bit; asleep, awake |Bit `p` of `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS_0` for pads 0 to 31, bit `p - 32` of `_1` for pads 32 to 46; bit `d` of `DIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS`. The pad is asleep while its status bit is 1, awake while it is 0 |[REG] hjson:745-748; reading RD9; `47 - 32 = 15` bits in `_1`
|A software clear of the status bit |An accepted write, in a cycle, to the status register holding the pad's bit, with that bit of the data at 0. The bit's byte is always enabled: a write whose byte enables leave out a byte holding a field of the register gets an error, so it is no accepted write (csr_fpv's error rule). Worked: `0xFBFFFFFF` to `_0` clears pad 26 alone; pad 40 is bit 8 of `_1` |[REG] `rw0c`; [RG]:74, 688-695; `0xFFFFFFFF - 2**26`
|The status bit's next value |What the bit holds in the next cycle: 0 if software clears it in this cycle; else 1 if it is 1 now, or if this cycle is a sleep entry with the pad's sleep enable at 1; else 0 |[RG]:810, 815, 884-900; readings RD9, RD37
|The set cycle, the held value |The set cycle: the last cycle before now with the status bit at 0, the sleep entry that set the bit. The held value: the pad's drive in the set cycle |[REG] hjson:837; reading RD9
|The sleep value |What an asleep pad drives, by the sleep mode taken: 0 drives (0, 1); 1 drives (1, 1); 2 drives (0, 0); 3 drives the held value |[REG] hjson:821-837; [TP] MioSleepMode0_A to MioOeSleepMode3_A
|The sleep mode taken |The pad's sleep mode in the set cycle; none if the pad was an owned JTAG pad in any cycle from the set cycle to now. A write to the sleep mode while the pad is held changes nothing: the new mode acts at the next sleep entry |[ToO]:78-79; [PG]:82; readings RD40, RD44
|The pad's attribute output |`mio_attr_o[p]` or `dio_attr_o[d]`, by field: `invert`, `virtual_od_en`, `pull_en`, `pull_select`, `keeper_en`, `schmitt_en`, `od_en`, `input_disable` (1 bit each), `slew_rate` (2), `drive_strength` (4) |[IF]:92, 96; reading RD7
|The pad's read-back |What a read of the pad's attribute register (`MIO_PAD_ATTR_p`, `DIO_PAD_ATTR_d`) returns in a cycle, by field: bits 0-7, 17:16, 23:20, mask `0x00F300FF`. The register is `hwext`: the pinmux supplies the value |[REG] hjson:551-619; [RG]:165; `0xFF + 0x30000 + 0xF00000`
|An attribute write |An accepted write to the pad's attribute register in a cycle its lock is 1 (open) |[REG] hjson:540-542
|The pad's last attribute write |The data of the last attribute write to the pad accepted before this cycle, since the last reset. With none: undefined, because the run's one reset starts from the init-value abstraction. A check makes no claim while the last attribute write is undefined |[PG]:27; run variants
|The reset attributes |0 in every field, except `pull_en` 1 on MIO 30 (IOC8, TAP strap 0): `0x4` |[REG] hjson:554; reading RD39
|A supported field |A field the pad library keeps (reading RD38). In this build (`prim_pad_attr`): every bidirectional type keeps `invert`, `virtual_od_en`, `pull_en`, `pull_select`, `input_disable` and `drive_strength` bit 0; InputStd keeps `invert`, `pull_en`, `pull_select` and `input_disable`; every other field reads 0. The per-type open drain sets of the top README are the chip library's, checked at chip level |[ToO]:175; readings RD4, RD38
|The register's lock |The bit of the `*_REGWEN` register that locks the register: 1 open, 0 closed; for `ALERT_TEST`, its own bit 31 |[REG]; `doc/registers.md:591`
|An accepted write |A write of data `v` to a register, accepted on `tl_i` in a cycle and answered with `d_error` 0; the register holds `v` from the next cycle (the attribute registers too: reading RD3) |csr_fpv field and error rules; reading RD37
|The correct command, response and data codes |The integrity codes over: a request's instruction type, address, opcode and mask; a response's opcode, size and error; the data. From the encoder both ends of every OpenTitan TL-UL link share (the shared interface primitive of TA-28) |[TLUL]:299-312; reading RD12
|A failed request |A request accepted on `tl_i` whose command code is not the correct command code of its fields, or a write whose data code is not the correct data code of its data. A read whose only fault is its data code is no failed request (reading RD12) |[TLUL]:299-304; reading RD12
|The fatal state |The design is in the fatal state in a cycle when a failed request was accepted since the last reset, in that cycle or before it |[REG] hjson:40
|An alert test |An accepted write to `ALERT_TEST`, in a cycle its lock is 1, with bit 0 of the data at 1 |`doc/registers.md:591-593`
|A ping, an alert event, `AlertLat` |A ping: a ping request on `alert_rx_i` in a cycle (assumption A3). An alert event: `alert_tx_o` moves in a cycle from (`alert_p`, `alert_n`) = (0, 1) to (1, 0), starting one alert event's four-phase handshake. `AlertLat`: the most cycles from a cause to its alert event, also the life of a ping's credit (xref:{tp}#tp_alert[alert]). No spec gives it: a bound the designers confirm |[ALERT]:129-169, ping testing, 219-225; reading RD13
|===

'''

[[defs_wakeup]]
==== Wakeup and USB wakeup

Per detector `w` (0 to 7), one step is one `clk_aon_i` cycle (200 kHz, 5 us; [TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:44). `EN`,
`MODE`, `FILTER`, `MIODIO`, `TH` (`CNT_TH`) are the fields of detector `w` as the AON logic holds them once a write has
landed (reading RD18); `PADSEL`, not synced (hjson:1119), is read as the register holds it.

[cols="2,7,2",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning |Source
|The watched value |`MIODIO` 0: `PADSEL` 0 gives 0, 1 gives 1, 2 to 48 give MIO pad number `PADSEL` minus 2 on `mio_in_i`, 49 to 63 give 0. `MIODIO` 1: 0 to 15 give DIO pad number `PADSEL` on `dio_in_i`, 16 to 63 give 0 |REQ_WKUP_01 to 03; hjson:1132-1135; RD15
|The sampled pad, the filtered pad |The sampled pad: the watched value sampled at each `clk_aon_i` edge, with no delay in the model. The filtered pad: with `FILTER` 0, the sampled pad; with `FILTER` 1, it takes a value once the sampled pad has had that value for 4 samples in a row, this one included, and holds otherwise. It runs whatever `EN` |REQ_WKUP_04, 05, 13; [ToO]:98-99; hjson:1073-1075; RD16
|A rise, a fall |A rise: the filtered pad was 0 in the cycle before and is 1. A fall: it was 1 and is 0 |hjson:1043, 1047
|The detector's mode |`MODE`, with 5, 6 and 7 read as 0 |REQ_WKUP_11; hjson:1039
|The run length |The number of cycles in a row, this one included, with `EN` 1 and the filtered pad at the mode's level: 1 in mode 3, 0 in mode 4 |REQ_WKUP_09, 10; [ToO]:104
|The detector's pattern, a detection |The pattern, by the detector's mode: 0 a rise; 1 a fall; 2 a rise or a fall; 3 and 4 the run length reaching `TH` + 1, and never a cause set while it is below `TH` (the detector fires once the level has held `TH` or `TH` + 1 cycles in a row: reading RD41). A detection: the pattern in a cycle with `EN` 1 |REQ_WKUP_06a to 12; RD41
|The enable held, the pad seen `k` late |The enable held at a cycle: `EN` is 1 in that cycle and in each of the `SmpLat` cycles after it. The pad seen `k` late: this cycle's `FILTER`, `MODE` and `EN` applied to the pad of `k` cycles before, `k` from 0 to `SmpLat`. The pinmux may see a pad level late, never early |RD16
|The start-up cycles |The first `SmpLat + 4` cycles after `rst_aon_ni` releases: the start value of the sampled and filtered pad is not in the spec, so the checks start once the filter is full (reading RD46) |RD46
|A cause set, a hardware write of the cause bit |A cause set: a hardware write of 1 to bit `w` of `WKUP_CAUSE`. A hardware write of the cause bit: any hardware write of that bit. Hardware may feed `q` back into `d` ([RG]:897-899): a write that leaves the bit as it is (1 to a bit at 1, 0 to a bit at 0, no clear landing) changes nothing, and no backward or stable check counts it |hjson:1153-1158 (`hrw`); [RG]:897-899
|The cause bit, any cause, the wakeup request |The cause bit: bit `w` of `WKUP_CAUSE` as the AON logic holds it. Any cause: at least one of the eight cause bits is 1. The wakeup request: `pin_wkup_req_o` |hjson:1158; [IF]:30
|An AON field write, a software clear of the cause bit, a landed clear |An AON field write: an accepted write (<<defs_pads>>), in a cycle its lock is 1, to the register of AON field `f`, with `v` the field's value (the locks: register_block). A software clear of the cause bit: an accepted write to `WKUP_CAUSE` with bit `w` of the data at 0, as for a sleep status bit. A landed clear: the cycle the register block's AON-side write of `WKUP_CAUSE` carries bit `w` at 0, where a clear lands ([TB] units) |hjson:1158; RD18
|A set as a clear lands |A cause set in the cycle a clear of the same bit lands |REQ_WKUP_17; [RG]:815, 884-900
|`SmpLat`, `WkLat`, `ReqLat`, `AonLat` |The most cycles from a pad level to the pattern logic; from a detection to its cause set, `SmpLat` included; from a change of any cause to the wakeup request; from an AON field write or a software clear of the cause bit to its landing. No spec gives a number ([PG]:106: a clear takes "a few uS"): bounds the designers confirm |RD16, RD18
|The module's port |The port of the USB wakeup module inside the pinmux that carries a given role |[ToO]:46-47
|===

Worked numbers (`python3 -c`): MIO pad `p` has `PADSEL` `p + 2`: MIO pad 0, 16 (IOB7), 46 give 2,
18, 48. `WKUP_DETECTOR` = `MODE + 8 FILTER + 16 MIODIO`: mode 4 filtered on MIO is `0x0C`, mode 2
on DIO `0x12`. 4 filter samples are 20 us, `TH` 255 is 1,275 us. USB_P, USB_N: DIO pads 0, 1.

'''

[[defs_lc]]
==== Life cycle, latch, straps and TAPs

Terms of the straps and TAPs checker; counts over the 16 values of a 4-bit input. Background: the design doc's
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#bg_lc[life cycle signals].

[cols="2,6,3",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning |Source
|`On`, `Off` |4'b1010 and 4'b0101; every bit toggles between them (On xor Off = 4'b1111) |[LC] `interfaces.md`:170; the package swaps them
|Is On (the strict test) |The input equals On: 1 value of 16 is On, the other 15 count as Off |[LC] `interfaces.md`:171
|Escalates (the escalation test) |The input is not Off: 15 values of 16 escalate, only 4'b0101 does not |[LC] `interfaces.md`:172
|Out of full reset, in full reset, an NDM reset |Out of full reset in a cycle: `rst_sys_ni` is 1. In full reset: it is 0. An NDM reset: `rst_ni` is 0 and `rst_sys_ni` is 1, `rst_aon_ni` free with it |reading RD24
|The strap pulse |A cycle with `strap_en_i` 1: one cycle, at most once between two full resets, never after an NDM reset |assumption A6 ([ToO]:155); RD29
|The TAP hold, scan mode |The TAP hold: `dft_hold_tap_sel_i` is 1. Scan mode: `scanmode_i` is at the True value of assumption A1 |[ToO]:139; [IF]:26; A1
|Steadily On |An input is steadily On in a cycle when, in each of the two cycles before it, the design was out of full reset and the input was On |RD23; [TP] `TapStrap_A` (hjson:729)
|Steadily Off |In each of the two cycles before it, the design was in full reset or the input was not On; a cycle in full reset counts as Off, the safe side |RD23; [LC] `lc_ctrl.hjson`:367
|Escalation steadily On, steadily Off |The same over `lc_escalate_en_i` with the escalation test: steadily On needs it to escalate in both cycles, out of full reset; steadily Off needs it Off, or full reset, in both |RD23; [LC] `interfaces.md`:172
|In its window |An input neither steadily On nor steadily Off (or, for escalation, neither of its two): it changed in the last two cycles; every rule leaves its outcome free there |RD23: "DV checks no cycle in between"
|[[defs_tap]]The latched debug enable |`pinmux_hw_debug_en_o`: the latched debug enable as the pinmux shows it |[IF]:21
|A life cycle clear, every clear steadily Off |A clear: `lc_hw_debug_clr_i` steadily On, or `lc_check_byp_en_i` steadily On, or escalation steadily On. Every clear steadily Off: those two inputs steadily Off and escalation steadily Off. Neither holds while an input is in its window and none is steadily On |[ToO]:158; [LC] `lc_ctrl.hjson`:353-355
|Strap pads |TAP strap 0: MIO 30 (IOC8); TAP strap 1: MIO 27 (IOC5); DFT strap 0: MIO 40 (IOR5); DFT strap 1: MIO 42 (IOR7); a rule reads strap pad `p` on `mio_in_i[p]` in the cycle it names |[TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:1784-1787
|The TAP straps |The model's strap 1 and strap 0, written in that order (01: strap 0 at 1) (xref:{tp}#tp_strap[strap]); a bit is a value or unknown, from a free cell until a sample sets it |[ToO]:119-127
|Every-cycle sampling, every-cycle sampling ruled out |Every-cycle sampling: `lc_dft_en_i` steadily On and the TAP hold 0. Ruled out: `lc_dft_en_i` steadily Off, or the TAP hold 1. Neither holds while `lc_dft_en_i` is in its window with the hold 0 |[ToO]:122-123, 139; RD22
|The TAP the straps name |00: none; 01: the life cycle TAP (`lc`); 10: the RISC-V TAP (`rv`); 11: the DFT TAP (`dft`) |[ToO]:134-137
|The TAP's gate: open, shut |`lc`: always open. `rv`: open when the latched debug enable is On, else shut. `dft`: open when `lc_dft_en_i` is steadily On, shut when it is steadily Off |[ToO]:135-137, 154, 157; [IF]:21
|A connected TAP, a cut TAP |Connected in a cycle: the straps name the TAP and its gate is open. Cut: the straps name another TAP or none, or its gate is shut. An unknown strap bit leaves both false |[ToO]:129-137
|The TAP's request, its response |`lc_jtag_o`, `rv_jtag_o`, `dft_jtag_o` (fields `tck`, `tms`, `tdi`, `trst_n`); `lc_jtag_i`, `rv_jtag_i`, `dft_jtag_i` (`tdo`, `tdo_oe`) |[IF]:22-24
|The JTAG pads as a request |`tck` MIO 38 (IOR3), `tms` 35 (IOR0), `tdi` 37 (IOR2), `trst_n` 39 (IOR4); the TDO pad is MIO 36 (IOR1) |[TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:1789-1793
|The JTAG pads taken, free |Taken in a cycle: some TAP is connected. Free: every TAP is cut. The pad testpoints guard their rules on MIO 35 to 39 with the JTAG pads free, through the owned JTAG pad (<<defs_pads>>) |RD28
|===

Worked numbers: `lc_dft_en_i` On in cycle 10 only: never steadily On; in its window in 11 and 12,
steadily Off from 13. A step to On in cycle 10: in its window in 11, steadily On from 12. Values
neither On nor Off: 14 (4'b0000 to 4'b0011, ...), fault values (RD50). Delays (RD23): a strap sample
lands in the next cycle; the TAP straps, the latched debug enable and the pads act on the TAP ports
in the same cycle; the RTL's registered TAP gates take 2 to 3 cycles.

=== register_block: the register block, by csr_fpv's generated checker

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Access types and reset values (xref:{reqs}#req_reg_01[`REQ_REG_01`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A lock opens at reset and closes once (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_01a[`REQ_LOCK_01a`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A lock opens at reset and closes once (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_01b[`REQ_LOCK_01b`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A lock opens at reset and closes once (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_01c[`REQ_LOCK_01c`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|A register with its lock closed holds (xref:{reqs}#req_lock_02[`REQ_LOCK_02`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

*Rule:* every field follows its [REG] access type and reset value on every request that is not a failed request (a
failed write: xref:{tp}#tp_bus[bus]); a lock is 1 (open) after reset, a write of 0 closes it, no write reopens it, and while it
is closed its registers ignore writes ([REG] hjson:27, the `regwen` keys; [RG]:74, 168, 297-305, 1105; [PG]:11, 57, 77).
*Run:* other plan: csr_fpv on `pinmux_reg_top`, `task_Csr_Main` and `task_Csr_BadIntegrity`; results in
its status doc; owner: the pinmux DV owner, who runs the link:../../csr_fpv/README.md[csr_fpv] project.

[%header,cols="2,3,4"]
|===
|Requirement |Decided in csr_fpv by |Not covered there: decided by
|REQ_REG_01 |field content and read data after requests that are not failed requests (`csr_field`, `csr_read`) |a failed write: bus _failed write changes nothing_; the attribute registers' storage (`hwext`): pad_attr _read-back changes only on a write_, _reset attributes_; the status bits' hardware set: pad_sleep
|REQ_LOCK_01a to REQ_LOCK_01c |the `rw0c` lock fields, `ALERT_TEST` bit 31 included (`csr_field`) |none
|REQ_LOCK_02 |`csr_regwen` |the attribute registers: regwen; a write accepted before its lock and landing in the AON domain after it: the wakeup detector testpoints
|bus _errors as the register checker predicts_ |`csr_errors` |failed requests: bus
|===

[[tp_reset_state]]
=== reset_state: every input reads 0 and every awake MIO pad is high-Z after reset

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|On the Earlgrey top: inputs read 0 after reset (xref:{reqs}#req_in_06[`REQ_IN_06`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|MIO pads high-Z after reset (xref:{reqs}#req_out_07[`REQ_OUT_07`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

*Follows from:* input select 0 reads 0 (REQ_IN_01), output select 2 is high-Z (REQ_OUT_03a and REQ_OUT_03b), and the reset values 0 and 2
([REG] hjson:466-472, 511-517) held until written (REQ_REG_01, csr_fpv). Premises: the pad awake and not an owned JTAG
pad; real reset values (`task_SelDefault_Main`, which has no init-value abstraction). On EG2 `eg2_default` replaces it.

[[tp_sleep_release]]
=== sleep_release: a pad whose status bit is 0 drives what its select names

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A released or never-held pad follows its selected drive (xref:{reqs}#req_slp_08[`REQ_SLP_08`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

*Follows from:* the output rows (REQ_OUT_01a to REQ_OUT_06b, xref:{tp}#tp_pad_output[pad_output]), whose condition, the pad
awake, is its status bit at 0. Premises: the pad follows its bit in the same cycle (reading RD9); the pad not an owned
JTAG pad (the JTAG pad testpoints).

[[tp_usb_module]]
=== usb_module: the USB wakeup module behaves as usbdev's spec says

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The module's behaviour (xref:{reqs}#req_usb_06[`REQ_USB_06`]) |(fill) |(fill)
|===

*Follows from:* usbdev's testbench tests `usbdev_aon_wake_resume`, `_reset` and `_disconnect`, owned by usbdev DV.
Premise: xref:{tp}#tp_usb_conn[usb_conn] holds.

References: the tests are at usbdev testplan:914-977. Their steps enable the AON/Wake module (:923, 942, 964),
which a 1 written to `suspend_req` activates (`usbdev.hjson`:1240-1242), and disable it (:929-930, 951-952, 974),
which `wake_ack` signals (`usbdev.hjson`:1250-1256). The same last steps (:929-930, 951-952, 974)
also check the device still connected, the DP pull-up enabled, or still disconnected after a VBUS
loss.

[[tp_jtag_ndm]]
=== jtag_ndm: an NDM reset keeps a connected RISC-V TAP

*Rule:* an NDM reset leaves the straps, the latch and a connected RISC-V TAP unchanged. Reset behaviour is out of scope for formal
(xref:../tb_arch/pinmux_tb_arch.adoc#reset_scope[TB architecture doc, restrictions]), so this testpoint has no checks or run.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A connected RISC-V TAP survives an NDM reset with every clear steadily Off (xref:{reqs}#req_tap_12[`REQ_TAP_12`]) |none |Not covered by formal: reset behaviour is out of scope
|===

[[witnesses]]
=== Consistency witnesses

One named input per pair of testpoints on one output, and per Never line whose output another
testpoint decides; each gets one answer, or none where a case is out of scope.

[%header,cols="3,5,1"]
|===
|Input |What each rule says |Answers
|_sleep over select_: pad 26 asleep in tie high, output select 81 |pad_output: no claim (asleep); pad_sleep: (1, 1) |one
|_entry with clear_: pad 26, a sleep entry with the pad's sleep enable at 1 and a software clear of its status bit in one cycle |pad_sleep: the status bit stays 0; pad_output: the selected drive |one
|_entry, no write_: pad 26, a sleep entry with the pad's sleep enable at 1 and no request on `tl_i` |pad_sleep: the status bit 1 in the next cycle (reading RD37); register_block: no claim, the status bits' hardware set being pad_sleep's (its REQ_REG_01 row) |one
|_keep over select_: pad 26 asleep in keep mode; output select written 2 |pad_output: no claim; pad_sleep: the held value |one
|_failed clear_: pad 26 asleep; a failed write of `0xFBFFFFFF` |pad_sleep: no software clear of the status bit, the status bit stays 1; bus: unchanged; register_block: no accepted write, so no `rw0c` clear |one
|_failed select write_: 81 to `MIO_OUTSEL_26` with an incorrect data code |bus: `d_error` 1, `MIO_OUTSEL_26` unchanged; register_block: no accepted write, the field keeps its value; pad_output: the selected drive of the old output select; alert: events until reset |one
|_locked attribute write_: `0x42` to pad 26 with its lock closed |regwen: unchanged; pad_attr: no attribute write, the pad's last attribute write unchanged |one
|_failed attribute write_: `0x1` to pad 26's attribute register, an incorrect command code |pad_attr: no attribute write; bus: unchanged; alert: events until reset |one
|_failed test write_: a test write with an incorrect command code |bus: error, no change; alert: no alert test, the fatal state sends events |one
|_pad 30 at reset_: Earlgrey top, no attribute write since the reset |pad_attr: the reset attributes `0x4`, the pad's attribute output equal to the read-back |one
|_owned pad_: pad 38's lock closed, a TAP connects; the input select of input 78 is 40 (pad 38); the output select of MIO 35 is 81 |regwen, pad_attr, pad_listen, pad_output: no claim (an owned JTAG pad); the JTAG pad testpoints decide |one
|_set then clear_: detector 0, a cause set at `t`, a landed clear at `t + 1` |wakeup _set lands_: 1 at `t + 1`; wakeup_sync _landed clear clears cause_: 0 at `t + 2`; wakeup_cause: 1 until the clear (each step one cycle: reading RD37) |one
|_detection, no write_: detector 0 enabled in mode 0, its pad rises, no write |wakeup: a cause set of bit 0, then the cause bit at 1; wakeup_sync: no AON field change, no landed clear of the cause bit; wakeup_cause: holds 1 |one
|_straps kept_: DEV, TAP straps 01, IOC5 toggles |strap: the TAP straps kept at 01; jtag: `lc_jtag_o` equals the JTAG pads as a request, the others 0 |one
|_straps ask DFT_: DEV, TAP straps 11, MIO 35 to 39 |the JTAG pads free (every TAP cut): the pad testpoints decide; jtag_pad is silent |one
|_transition clear_: a transition clears the latched debug enable in 33, TAP straps 10 |latch: the latched debug enable Off from 33; jtag: `rv_jtag_o` 0 from 33 |one
|===

An unreachable cover means an over-constrained environment until triaged.

[%header,cols="3,5,2"]
|===
|Cover |Shows |Testpoint
|_every select class_, _peripheral turns a pad around_ |each select class on every input and pad; an enable toggles on a selected output |pad_listen, pad_output
|_entry with each mode_, _release_ |sleep entries with sleep modes 0 to 3, and a software clear of the status bit |pad_sleep
|_open attribute write_, _lock closed_ |an attribute write and its read-back; a lock written 0, then its register written |pad_attr, regwen
|_failed request_, _alert test_, _ping_ |each cause gives an alert event on `alert_tx_o` |bus, alert
|===
